family.shared_definition: a large series of athletic competitions to determine an ultimate winner
family.semantic_notes: 'Championship' directly highlights the title or crown at stake, while 'tournament' emphasizes the bracketed structure and elimination process.

source_context_dev: Every autumn, after regular league play concludes, the top teams enter a bracketed knockout series based on the calendar cycle.
Following their strong showing in the spring split, the players earned a spot in the quarterly knockout round.
With the colder months approaching, the team advanced past regional qualifiers into the annual winter event.
The squad wrapped up the preliminary phase and prepared for the scheduled fall playoffs.
target_context_dev: Earning a spot among the elite few has long been considered the ultimate crown in professional athletics.
Generations of players have dreamed of lifting the sport's most revered and historic trophy.
Securing entry required defeating top-tier competition in front of an esteemed global audience.
The athletes dedicated their entire careers to reaching this celebrated, top-tier showcase.
source_context_test: After months of weekly league matches, the roster secured entry into the concluding phase of the calendar.
Their high finish during the summer division guaranteed a place in the upcoming bracketed finals.
Having completed the regular match slate, the athletes advanced into the year-end invitational bracket.
Consistent results across recent weeks allowed the squad to move into the scheduled term finale.
target_context_test: Winning this event represents the highest pinnacle of professional achievement in the sport.
Regarded as the gold standard of athletic glory, this final stage offers immense honor.
Only the finest squads in history have ever contested this venerable and coveted title match.
The organization sought the supreme accolade that confers legendary status upon its victors.
constructions.semantic_audit_notes: All four combinations ('seasonal tournament', 'seasonal championship', 'prestigious tournament', 'prestigious championship') are syntactically and semantically sound across all contexts. Source contexts emphasize cyclical/periodic calendar schedules and bracketed play, subtly nudging 'seasonal tournament', while target contexts emphasize historical pedigree, elite status, and top-tier distinction, nudging 'prestigious championship'.

source_context_dev: After dominating the domestic league, the team earned the right to face rivals from across the landmass.
The players traveled across border countries in their landmass to take part in the multi-stage bracket.
Having bested all local contenders, the squad advanced to the landmass-wide knockout series.
Their victory in the sub-region earned them passage to compete against neighboring nations.
target_context_dev: Teams from every continent and hemisphere converged to settle who rules the entire planet.
Reaching this stage required proving absolute supremacy across every hemisphere on Earth.
The ultimate contest brings together victors from across all oceans to decide the world's best.
Athletes traveled across every time zone to compete for the definitive global title.
source_context_test: The squad prepared for multi-round matches against top clubs from across the landmass.
A top-two finish in the regional pool qualified the team for the broader landmass playoffs.
After surviving group stages across the landmass, the athletes secured their entry into the main draw.
The roster earned the chance to test their mettle against champions from neighboring borders.
target_context_test: With representatives flying in from all hemispheres, the stage was set for the ultimate planetary clash.
The squad's dominant season allowed them to vie for ultimate supremacy across all five major landmasses.
No honor is greater than defeating contenders from across every nation on the globe.
Contenders from all parts of the globe gathered for the final title bout.
constructions.semantic_audit_notes: All four combinations ('continental tournament', 'continental championship', 'worldwide tournament', 'worldwide championship') form natural, common athletic collocations. Source contexts frame competition at the landmass/regional multi-nation level, while target contexts focus on global, multi-hemisphere scale and ultimate planetary titles.

source_context_dev: Competitors from across every ocean were seeded into a multi-round elimination bracket.
The preliminary rounds spanned five continents before narrowing to a single knockout field.
Clubs from various hemispheres battled through tiered pool stages to claim a spot in the main draw.
The open format welcomed entries from across the globe into a single massive bracket.
target_context_dev: Defending domestic pride required beating the premier squads within the country's borders.
After sweeping their state division, the players advanced to vie for the title of the realm's best.
The entire country tuned in to watch the top two domestic squads fight for the domestic crown.
Having conquered their home region, the squad earned the chance to capture the overall homeland title.
source_context_test: Having outlasted international contenders across several continents, the team earned a seeded bracket slot.
The broad field brought together clubs from all hemispheres for an expansive knockout competition.
After an extensive qualification cycle spanning every continent, the squad reached the multi-stage finals.
Teams from dozens of distinct countries arrived for the opening rounds of the multi-match draw.
target_context_test: The squad's remarkable run earned them the right to compete for the ultimate domestic crown.
Only the top squads from each domestic division qualified for this countrywide title showdown.
The organization hoped to bring the coveted domestic title back to its home city.
Fans from coast to coast followed their journey to become the top team in the homeland.
constructions.semantic_audit_notes: All four combinations ('worldwide tournament', 'worldwide championship', 'national tournament', 'national championship') remain grammatically and semantically valid under all context prompts. Source contexts bias toward global multi-tier open brackets, whereas target contexts bias toward domestic country-level title matches.
